transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right... I'm just having a little bit of trouble at work lately. I do bookkeeping, and, well... I guess I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again. 

I know it's probably just me wanting to be a good employee and be thorough, but... I end up staying at work for hours after everyone else leaves. Even when I already checked everything and I know the numbers are right, I just... I get this really awful feeling that if I don't do it just one more time, something really bad is going to happen, and... and it'll be all my fault. 

Does that make sense? I'm sorry, I hope that's the kind of thing I'm supposed to talk about here.
Do you have these repeating thoughts or feelings of needing to check things when you're not at work?

Um... I'm not really sure? I haven't... I haven't really noticed it as much at home, I don't think. 

I mean, I try to keep my apartment nice and orderly, just like anyone would, you know? But... the really overwhelming part is definitely just with the bookkeeping. I really try to leave all that stress at the office so I'm not a bother to anyone else when I get home. 

Is... is that normal? To mostly just have it happen at your job? I hope it's okay that I don't really have a good example for when I'm not at work.
Do you feel like you have to perform certain actions in a specific way or a certain number of times to feel okay?

Um, yeah, I guess that kind of goes back to what I was trying to explain earlier? About the spreadsheets... I don't know if I have a specific exact *number* of times I have to do it, but I definitely just have to keep going over the same calculations again and again until it finally feels okay. 

Like I mentioned, I'll stay for hours after everyone else is gone, just re-doing them. Even when I look right at the screen and I know I already checked it and the math is perfect... I just get so scared that if I don't run the numbers just *one* more time, or if I don't check them in the exact right order, I'll have missed something. And then something terrible will happen to the company and it'll be all my fault. 

I just really want to be reliable and do a good job, you know? I hope that answers your question... am I explaining that okay?
Do you feel like your need to repeatedly check the spreadsheets is interfering with other parts of your life?

Um... well, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I really don't want to complain, because I know everyone gets busy and has to make sacrifices for their job sometimes... 

But, um... I did actually miss a filing deadline recently because I was still checking the numbers. My boss had to call me in for a formal meeting about it. I felt so terrible, I really didn't mean to let anyone down. I just wanted it to be perfect, you know? 

And... well, I used to sing in a choir, and I volunteered at the youth center, but... I haven't been making it to those lately. I just can't seem to get out of the office on time anymore. I feel really bad about missing them, but I just have to make sure my work is right first. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee or an unreliable person... Is it normal to struggle with balancing things like that?
Do you feel anxious or upset when you're unable to repeat your checking behavior?

Um... well, yes. I guess I do get kind of... worked up? I try really hard not to let anyone see it, because I don't want to be a bother or seem unprofessional. 

But like I was saying about how I just can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations... if something happens and I *can't* stay late to do it, or if my boss tells me I have to log off right then... I get this really awful, tight feeling in my chest. 

Even when I know I already checked them, if I can't do it just that one more time, I get so scared. I just feel so completely sure that something terrible is going to happen to the company because of a mistake I missed, and it'll be all my fault. So I just... I really have to do it, just to make that feeling stop. 

I hope I don't sound too dramatic or... or crazy for getting upset over something like that. Does that make sense?
How much distress do you feel when you're unable to repeat your checking behavior?

Um... well, it's... I mean, I try really hard to just push through it, you know? I don't want to make a big deal out of it. But... it's pretty bad. 

I guess on a scale, it would be... maybe really high? Like, it feels almost unbearable sometimes. My heart races and I can't focus on anything else until I can get back to the computer and check it again. I know that probably sounds like I'm overreacting, and I really try to just be normal about it, but... the panic just takes over. 

I really don't want to sound like I can't handle my job, because I promise I'm a hard worker. I just... I get really, really overwhelmed if I can't make sure everything is perfect. Is it okay that I feel that way? I mean, is that something you hear a lot from people?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family or friends due to your need to repeatedly check your work?

Um... well, honestly... I guess I kind of already mentioned some of it? I really hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question right. 

But, um, like I said before... I did have that issue at work where I missed the filing deadline and had that formal meeting with my boss. And... and I haven't been going to my choir rehearsals or volunteering at the youth center lately. I just... I can't seem to leave the office when I'm supposed to, because I'm stuck checking the numbers. 

So, I guess... yes? It is affecting things. My choir friends have been asking where I am, and I just tell them I'm busy with work, which is true, but... I feel awful lying by omission, you know? I hate letting people down. I just want to be reliable for everyone. Do you think they'll understand if I ever figure out how to explain it to them?
What is it that you are specifically afraid will happen if you don't check the spreadsheets one more time?

Um... well, it's... I know it probably sounds really silly, because I literally just checked them. I promise I know how to do my job, and I know the numbers match. 

But... it's like this thought just forces its way into my head. I'll be looking right at the screen, and my brain will just say, what if you missed one hidden mistake? Like in the payroll, or the taxes... and what if somebody's paycheck doesn't go through because of me? Or what if the whole firm gets in trouble with the IRS or something? 

I really do try to push the thought away, I swear I do. I tell myself it's fine, but... it just comes right back. It's almost like I can't trust my own eyes anymore. I just want to make sure everyone gets paid and the company is safe, you know? I don't want to cause any problems for anyone. Does that... does that make sense, why I'd be so worried about that?
Do you ever feel the need to repeat certain behaviors or rituals when you're not working?

Um... no, not really. I mean... I don't think so? 

I really try to keep everything together when I'm at home. I don't want to be, you know, difficult to live with or anything. So I don't have any routines like the checking I do at work. I just try to relax and be normal. 

I guess I'm mostly just so tired from work that I don't have the energy for anything else anyway. But no, I don't think I do anything weird at home. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. Is it normal that it only really happens at the office?
Have you had to turn down social invitations or opportunities because of your need to check your work?

Um... yeah. I know I kind of touched on this a little bit earlier? I hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know. 

But, um... yes. Like I mentioned before, I've had to stop going to my choir rehearsals, and I haven't been making it to my youth-center commitments either. I just... I can't get out of the office on time because I'm so caught up making sure the numbers are right. And it's not just social things, it's like I said about missing that filing deadline and getting called into that formal meeting with my boss. 

I really, really don't want to be a flake, and I feel terrible turning my friends down when they ask me to do things. It's just... I can't seem to leave the building until I know everything is safe and correct. I'm really trying my best to keep up with everyone, I promise. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm making sense.
Do you think your need to repeatedly check the spreadsheets is affecting your overall quality of life?

Um... yes, I... I guess it really is. I mean, I don't want to complain, because I know I'm lucky to have my job and everything, but... it's just getting really hard. 

Like I was saying about the choir rehearsals and the youth center... I really loved doing those things. They were the best part of my week. And now I just... I can't do them anymore. I feel awful about letting people down. I try so hard to be reliable, but I just can't leave the office. 

And then... well, the thing with my boss. Missing that filing deadline and having to sit in that formal meeting... that was really embarrassing. I felt like such a failure. I'm supposed to be good at this, you know? I'm trying so hard to do everything right, and it feels like I'm just messing everything up instead. 

I really don't want to be a burden on anyone, or make it seem like I'm not trying. I promise I'm trying. It's just... I guess it is affecting my life a lot more than I wanted to admit. Is it okay that I'm struggling this much with it? I hope I'm not sounding too dramatic.
Is there something specific that you are afraid of happening if you make a mistake in the bookkeeping?

Um... well, it's a little silly, I guess. I mean, I know I shouldn't think this way, and I really try not to, but... 

It's just that, even when I've checked everything and I *know* the numbers match up perfectly, I get this... this thought. It just sort of jumps into my head that maybe I missed one tiny, hidden mistake somewhere in the payroll or the taxes. And if I did, then maybe someone's paycheck won't go through, or the whole firm could get in trouble because of me. 

I know it sounds crazy, and I really do try to push the thought away. I tell myself I'm being ridiculous and that I did it right. But it just comes right back. It's like I suddenly can't even trust my own eyes anymore. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely incompetent. I promise I'm actually really careful, and I don't want you to think I'm bad at my job. I just... I worry a lot about letting people down. Is it normal to get stuck on a thought like that? I'm sorry if that's a weird answer.
Are you feeling like your need to check the spreadsheets is impacting your relationships with family or friends outside of work?

Um... yes. I... I'm so sorry, I know I keep bringing up the same examples. I really hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're asking for. 

But... yeah, it really is affecting my relationships. Like I was saying earlier about the choir rehearsals and the youth-center commitments... those were the main ways I spent time with my friends. And since I've stopped making it to them because I just... I can't get out of the office on time... I haven't really been seeing anyone. 

I feel terrible about it. I really don't want them to think I'm ignoring them, because I care about them so much. I'm trying my best to send them texts and keep in touch, I promise I am. But between staying late every night and then... well, like I said, missing that filing deadline and getting called into that formal meeting at work... everything just feels so overwhelming right now. 

I don't want to sound like a bad friend. I really am trying to hold everything together. Am I answering your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you feeling like your need to check the spreadsheets is significantly impacting your daily life or overall well-being?

Um... yeah, I guess it is. I... I know I keep talking about the same things, and I really hope you don't mind me repeating myself again. I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But, um, yes, it's taking up a lot of my time. Like I mentioned before, I've completely stopped going to my choir rehearsals and the youth center because I just can't seem to leave the office when I'm supposed to. I feel awful about it, I really do. I don't want anyone to think I'm flaky or undependable. 

And then... well, the thing at work. Missing that filing deadline and having to go to that formal meeting with my boss... that really showed me that this is becoming a bigger issue than I wanted to admit. I'm so sorry, I know I've said all this already. I just... I really want to do a good job, and I'm trying my hardest to fix it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just making excuses for myself.
Are you feeling like your need to check the spreadsheets is making it difficult for you to enjoy or participate in activities you used to find pleasurable?

Um... yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I really don't want to sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry for bringing up the exact same things again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.

But, um... yes, the things I used to really love doing... I just haven't been able to do them lately. Like the choir rehearsals and volunteering at the youth center. I used to really look forward to those, but I just... I can't seem to get out of the office on time anymore to make it to them. I feel so guilty about it, like I'm letting everyone down. I promise I'm not doing it on purpose. 

And, um, with work... missing that filing deadline and having that formal meeting... it's just making it really hard to enjoy much of anything right now because I'm so worried about messing up again. I really am trying to get back on track, though. I don't want you to think I've just given up on everything. Is it okay that I used those same examples again? I hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.

target_item.manifestation: I missed a filing deadline and got called into a formal meeting at work, and I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and youth-center commitments because I can’t get out of the office on time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the checking behavior on relationships with family or friends outside of work, which relates to social and functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Um... yes. I... I'm so sorry, I know I keep bringing up the same examples. I really hope it's okay that I'm repeating myself again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're asking for. 

But... yeah, it really is affecting my relationships. Like I was saying earlier about the choir rehearsals and the youth-center commitments... those were the main ways I spent time with my friends. And since I've stopped making it to them because I just... I can't get out of the office on time... I haven't really been seeing anyone. 

I feel terrible about it. I really don't want them to think I'm ignoring them, because I care about them so much. I'm trying my best to send them texts and keep in touch, I promise I am. But between staying late every night and then... well, like I said, missing that filing deadline and getting called into that formal meeting at work... everything just feels so overwhelming right now. 

I don't want to sound like a bad friend. I really am trying to hold everything together. Am I answering your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are causing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life
doctor.question: Are you feeling like your need to check the spreadsheets is significantly impacting your daily life or overall well-being?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I missed a filing deadline and got called into a formal meeting at work, and I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and youth-center commitments because I can’t get out of the office on time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the checking behavior is significantly impacting daily life or overall well-being, which directly relates to the functional impairment caused by the symptoms.

patient.answer:
Um... yeah, I guess it is. I... I know I keep talking about the same things, and I really hope you don't mind me repeating myself again. I just want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

But, um, yes, it's taking up a lot of my time. Like I mentioned before, I've completely stopped going to my choir rehearsals and the youth center because I just can't seem to leave the office when I'm supposed to. I feel awful about it, I really do. I don't want anyone to think I'm flaky or undependable. 

And then... well, the thing at work. Missing that filing deadline and having to go to that formal meeting with my boss... that really showed me that this is becoming a bigger issue than I wanted to admit. I'm so sorry, I know I've said all this already. I just... I really want to do a good job, and I'm trying my hardest to fix it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just making excuses for myself.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's symptoms are causing significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of life
doctor.question: Are you feeling like your need to check the spreadsheets is making it difficult for you to enjoy or participate in activities you used to find pleasurable?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: I missed a filing deadline and got called into a formal meeting at work, and I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and youth-center commitments because I can’t get out of the office on time.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the need to check spreadsheets is making it difficult to enjoy or participate in pleasurable activities. This relates to how the symptoms are impacting the patient's daily functioning and activities (choir rehearsals, youth-center commitments), which falls under Functional Impairment.

patient.answer:
Um... yeah, I suppose so. I mean, I really don't want to sound like a broken record, and I'm so sorry for bringing up the exact same things again. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.

But, um... yes, the things I used to really love doing... I just haven't been able to do them lately. Like the choir rehearsals and volunteering at the youth center. I used to really look forward to those, but I just... I can't seem to get out of the office on time anymore to make it to them. I feel so guilty about it, like I'm letting everyone down. I promise I'm not doing it on purpose. 

And, um, with work... missing that filing deadline and having that formal meeting... it's just making it really hard to enjoy much of anything right now because I'm so worried about messing up again. I really am trying to get back on track, though. I don't want you to think I've just given up on everything. Is it okay that I used those same examples again? I hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of repeatedly checking spreadsheets, fear of making mistakes, and significant distress when unable to perform these behaviors are consistent with Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD).
